name: Fort Ville-Marie
scope: A circa-1660 archaeological reconstruction of Fort Ville-Marie at Pointe à Callière, Montréal, with four timber bastions, palisade curtains, central yard and a representative chapel, guardhouse, workshop, documented 1658 well and domestic ranges. It is a dated preview of the fort before abandonment.

originalReview.notes: Public-domain 1884 bird’s-eye reconstruction, used for relative arrangement of modest gabled ranges around a yard. Excavated timber-bastion geometry takes precedence.

review.notes: Started with Qualla. The local Morin scan matches the exact independent file record, and the City Archives confirm his 1884 volume. The model uses the McGill manuscript’s written catalog description. The Bourdon scan, later street schemes and photographs of the museum were excluded.
